facts.fact: 全车人都去万圣节游行：David 用德语唱《99 Luftballons》；Annie 用塔罗给 Cris 算（三剑穿心→再抽又是背后插更多剑的倒吊人）；Kurt 愿为孩子模仿 Vincent Price。
facts.anchor: Everyone on the bus was going to the Halloween parade. David sang “99 Luftballons” in German as we crossed town. Annie had her tarot cards in her bag and read for Cris, who asked if she should break up with her girlfriend. She drew a heart with three swords stuck in it, so she asked if she could pick another one, and got a guy, face down, with even more swords in his back. Kurt and Darryl and Joe had all their gear, and a kid sitting in front of them asked if they could play “Thriller.” Kurt was willing to do his best Vincent Price for him.

facts.fact: 第九大道下车即有卡车甩下一块动物脂肪；Bianca：「那是骨头卡车——开往胶水城。」
facts.anchor: “That’s the bone truck,” Bianca said. “En route to glue city.”

facts.fact: Bianca 穿的是她的牛仔夹克；扮装没劲——「今年没这个心，我希望 Star 在这儿。」
facts.anchor: She stuck out a stockinged leg. I shrugged. She sang a few bars of “What’s Love Got to Do with It?” and then sighed. “My heart’s just not in it this year. I wish Star were here.”

facts.fact: Julie 问她明天生日想做什么——她决定：想见 Claude。
facts.anchor: “I wanna see Claude,” I decided.

facts.fact: David 上劲后拿起砖头把门锁砸到铰链脱落；Darryl 被迷住：「你最近在练吗？」
facts.anchor: But David brought the brick down against the lock again and again until the hinge fell off. “Easy.”

facts.fact: 众人接上音箱与合成器（Kurt 带来心爱的 theremin）：Mucous Membrane 开演——「我们在你体内，一二三四」。
facts.anchor: “WE ARE MUCOUS MEMBRANE WE ARE INSIDE YOU ONE TWO THREE FOUR—”

facts.fact: 音乐是致密、黑暗的：能跳舞的不和谐音、从被亵渎教堂里拆出的管风琴、僵尸朋克；噪音穿透血管填满头脑，只剩共舞之乐。
facts.anchor: It was dissonance you could dance to, it was an organ ripped out of a desecrated church, it was zombie punk.

facts.fact: 有人在她耳边说「我叫了警察」——是 Rick（他一直站在她身后看着他们跳舞）；他吼着要她带朋友滚、警察马上到。
facts.anchor: Rick started yelling at me to get my fucking friends out of here

facts.fact: 她感到空气变了——不是因 Rick：一阵可听见的静默，像有人要喊「惊喜」之前的那种。
facts.anchor: There was a hush you could hear, if you knew what you were listening for, like the kind before someone yells surprise.

facts.fact: 接着：TZZT——断电。她把注意力放到嗡鸣上（像楼下收音机），越听越大声，像旋钮在转：声音、音乐、笑声、低语交织——像《Got to Give It Up》里混在底下的派对声。
facts.anchor: Instead—TZZT.

facts.fact: 她借 Silverman 的语气讲 theremin 原理：不靠触碰、靠感知附近的「在场」发声——所以听起来像外星，其实由很近的东西控制。
facts.anchor: “It makes sounds without being touched by sensing presences nearby. That’s why it sounds so alien, but it’s actually controlled by something very close.”

facts.fact: Rick 破防：「这只是《My Favorite Martian》，小孩子玩意儿」——随后收音机里漏出一声「I—」，他失焦：这是《Good Vibrations》，「那是她最喜欢的专辑；我们小时候躺在地下室地板上听收音机。」
facts.anchor: “Okay, so it’s ‘Good Vibrations.’ I used to listen to that with…That was her favorite album; we were kids and we used to listen to the radio on the basement floor.”

facts.fact: 他想用对讲机稳住局面，可对讲机的声音越来越响（笑声、尖叫、非人的片段）；他把对讲机扔向冷冻库，声音却已无处不在。
facts.anchor: In a final effort to remain in control, he ripped his walkie-talkie out of his belt and started to say his partner’s name—“Julian”—but the walkie-talkie started to speak, the voices louder, more insistent, the radio dial turning faster. It got louder: laughter and screams, some snatches of sound not entirely human. Rick threw the walkie-talkie toward the freezer, but the sound was everywhere now, amplified, filling the room.

facts.fact: 直到 SLAM：冷冻库门被炸开，挂锁撞墙碎裂飞到他们脚边；Rick 探头一看后退：「不。」
facts.anchor: Until—SLAM.

facts.fact: 库内明显没上次冷——像温水浴，她感到舒适、被欢迎；短路损坏了笼子（金属熔化、网格缺口）；除后排几行，格子仍填满并标着地址。
facts.anchor: It was noticeably less cold than the last time I was there. It felt like a warm bath, and I felt good. I was welcome.

facts.fact: 她想读完每一个地址以确认 Mark 不在其中——尽管她心底最孤独的角落早知道他不在了；他走了。
facts.anchor: I wanted to read every single address until I was certain that Mark wasn’t in there, even though I knew, in the loneliest corner of my heart, that he wasn’t anywhere. He was gone.

facts.fact: 读地址的过程不再只关于 Mark：每一格都住过某个人；她认出母亲带着她搬过的街、好约会与烂约会的街、朋友住过的街——追索公司的版图，最后画出的是自己人生的地图。
facts.anchor: As I traced where Manhattan Remediation had been, I stopped thinking about them and started making a map in my head of my own life.

facts.fact: 77 年大停电的经验：要先过一会儿才意识到不只是自己家没交电费——「事情先发生在你身上，之后你才明白它对所有人都发生了。」
facts.anchor: Things happen to you before you realize they’re happening to everyone.

facts.fact: 她的感受：一种开放感——像陌生人靠在你肩上睡着、你不挪动让他睡；像是没有人跟别人不同、发生在别人身上的迟早轮到你，而这并不可怕；人们相互依赖如此明显，「唯一该害怕的，是紧抱『不需要任何人』幻想的人」。
facts.anchor: We depend on one another to survive in such obvious ways that the only people who should be scared are the ones who hold tight to their fantasy of needing no one.

facts.fact: 「然后我又只是我」：身体只属于自己；鬼被释放了——它们无处不在，本就该如此；她握不住它们，没人能。
facts.anchor: And then I was just me. My body was only mine. The ghosts were released, because they were everywhere, as they should be. I couldn’t hold them—no one could.

facts.fact: Rick 倒在远处地板上抱着自己、散发着「某种急迫不对的气味」、白脸避开耻辱的聚光灯——这正是 Rick 最不想看/触/闻/知道的；她想起 François 失禁的景象与 Leon 的话；「擦掉会留下污痕——residue；压抑悲伤，它会浮回来更可怕」；「生活对他这类人太脏乱，而现在他就躺在自己的脏乱里」。
facts.anchor: This, I realized, was exactly what Rick didn’t want: didn’t want to see, to touch, to hear, or to smell or to know in any way at all. I saw him, and I saw myself, too, and I knew why I was so obsessed with putting a stop to what he was doing. Silverman, too, wanted to wipe it all clean. He should have seen through that fascist rhetoric, but then, sometimes it’s really more about character than history. My mother used to say that about being a communist and a Jew—you share a past, so what, what are you going to build from there? And I felt profoundly sad for both of them in that moment, these people who refused to be near anyone else’s feelings but also wanted to shut down their own, to make it all clean. Wipe it away and you leave a smudge. Residue. Push down sadness and it floats back up, bloated and more terrible than before. You can deny the reality of other people only if you refuse to know what it means to be a person, to close your eyes to sickness and death and difference only to end up denying your own. Living was too messy for people like him, and now here he was, lying in his own mess.

facts.fact: 警察到场：「又一位送 Bellevue 的」「今晚第三个了」；把他架起问「你嗑了什么」；被拖走时他眼里空掉。
facts.anchor: “All right, buddy.” They hoisted him up. “Whatddya take?”

facts.fact: 她判定这些不是重罪（可能进 The Tombs 或 Bellevue）；「他越过了自己十年加固的边界，发现它终究保护不了他。也许他会学到，也许会更糟——但我们不再是彼此的问题了。」
facts.anchor: He had crossed a boundary he had spent a decade fortifying and found out that it didn’t protect him after all. Maybe he’d learn, or maybe he’d just get worse. But we weren’t going to be each other’s problem anymore.

facts.fact: 朋友们在街上等她，Tanya 催着去游行——Julie 答：「我们就是游行。」
facts.anchor: “We are the parade,” Julie said.
